properties.name: MEASURED 2026-10-11: once a branch holds the design, the guard's `copy` says only "this branch holds the design; N items in flight" and takes everything — writes made meanwhile by another session (a claude.ai chat's brainstorm decision and two accepted requirements) rode into the fix PR's copy with no line naming them; the guard distinguishes other HOLDERS, not other WRITERS, and --adopt is asked only when nobody holds
properties.source: who:ajs via the dev_reflow2 hub session; tools/reflow2_design_copy.py and flo2.io's call log
properties.statement: OBSERVED while taking the copy for the acceptance-reset fix (reflow2 #719), 2026-10-11 ~04:30 UTC. This session held the design (claim on proj:reflow2, note "design PR: fix/…"). Between the hold and the copy, Anthony's claude.ai chat wrote three nodes into reflow2's hosted design through flo2.io (dec:idea-how-is-a-decision-that-rests-on-numbers-held-to-keeping-its-math, req:a-decision-names-the-quantities-it-rests-on-each-with-its-provenance, req:a-decision-written-with-unsourced-numbers-is-flagged-in-the-write-reply — flo2.io's call log, client Claude-User, 03:00–03:04). `copy` reported "This branch … holds the design; 31 item(s) are in flight" and wrote all 31; nothing named the 12 that were not this PR's. They were noticed only because the copy's diff was read by hand, and the PR body then said so. WHY, read in the script: judge() has three branches — other holders (refuse, or --adopt), nobody holds (refuse, or --adopt), this branch holds (take everything). "In flight" is computed as live-minus-main with holds removed, never by writer, because the store records who wrote (the contributor), not on which branch, and here the writer was the same person (who:ajs) through two doors. WHAT IT COSTS: a design PR can carry another session's intent without saying so; the one-PR-at-a-time rule holds for PRs but not for writes made outside any PR while one is open — which is now the ordinary case, since the chat door writes to the same hosted design. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: `copy` listing, per in-flight item, the acting agent or client (the gateway records both on every write), and saying which items were written by a different agent than the one holding, so the PR author decides with eyes open; or a hold that names its seat/agent and a copy that flags items by other agents. Recorded as a finding, not a defect: the rule as written is kept; the gap is in what the copy says. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
